How hit chance and damage per round work in 5e

An attack hits when the d20 plus your attack bonus equals or beats the target's Armor Class. A natural 1 always misses and a natural 20 always hits, so even the best bonus tops out at 95% and the worst still lands 5% of the time. Each point of attack bonus or AC moves the odds by 5%.

Damage per round is each attack's chance to hit times its average damage, added up. A critical hit rolls the damage dice twice but adds the flat bonus only once, so a crit with 1d8 + 3 averages 12, not 15.

Advantage, disadvantage, and crits

With advantage you roll two d20s and keep the higher, with disadvantage the lower. The effect is biggest in the middle: an attack that needs an 11 goes from 50% to 75% with advantage, and down to 25% with disadvantage.

Need on the d20NormalAdvantageDisadvantage
2 or higher95%99.8%90.3%
5 or higher80%96%64%
8 or higher65%87.8%42.3%
11 or higher50%75%25%
14 or higher35%57.8%12.3%
17 or higher20%36%4%
20 only5%9.8%0.3%

The same table gives crit chances: 5% on a 20, 10% on 19–20 (the Champion's Improved Critical), and 15% on 18–20 (Superior Critical), rising to 9.8%, 19%, and 27.8% with advantage.

Is the −5 / +10 trade-off worth it?

Some options let you take a penalty to your attack roll for extra damage on a hit. Losing 5 to hit costs a quarter of your hits; gaining 10 damage on each one that lands usually more than makes up for it against low AC. A rough rule, ignoring crits: it pays when your normal chance to hit is at least 25% plus your average hit damage divided by 40. A greatsword at 2d6 + 4 (11 on average) needs about a 53% chance to hit before the penalty. Advantage and Bless push the line in its favor. Against a very high AC it pays again, because only the crit range can hit and a crit lands whatever the penalty. The calculator works out the exact ACs where it pays.

What the options cover

  • Great Weapon Fighting rerolls a 1 or 2 on a two-handed melee weapon's damage dice: about +1.33 average on a 2d6 greatsword and +0.83 on a 1d12 greataxe.
  • Extra dice on a crit covers the barbarian's Brutal Critical and the half-orc's Savage Attacks (both melee only: tick Ranged on a bow or crossbow row to leave them off it).
  • Once per turn, first hit is for Sneak Attack, Colossus Slayer, a Divine Smite you plan to spend, or any bonus that lands once. It goes on the first attack that hits and doubles its dice on a crit.
  • Bonuses on every hit such as rage damage, Hunter's Mark, or Improved Divine Smite go into the attack's damage, like 1d8 + 5 + 1d6.
  • Times is how often you make that attack in a round: 2 for Extra Attack, plus 1 for an off-hand or bonus action attack on its own row. Set a row to 0 to keep it listed without counting it.

Works with

Load a character from the Character Builder to fill in its attacks, Extra Attack, crit range, Lucky, and Sneak Attack, then print those attacks as cut-out Feature & Item Cards. Look up a monster's AC in the Bestiary, and run the fight in the Initiative Tracker.
